summary: Backend-only verification of the new customer-facing Payment Recovery Email (services/payment_recovery_email.py) and its wiring into routers/payments.py's invoice.payment_failed webhook branch. All 5 tests in tests/test_stripe_invoice_payment_failed.py pass (note: review_request mentioned 6 tests — file contains 5 and covers every requested behavior; no coverage gap). Independently verified render_text() and render_html() include plan name, $X.XX amount, and portal_url as an href/CTA. Prior batch behaviors (dev_users payment_failed flag, founder alert guard='stripe_dunning', invoice.paid recovery clear, /payments/my-plan payment_failed field) all still pass alongside the new customer email — no regression.
critical_code_review_comments: services/payment_recovery_email.py: clean, mirrors welcome_email.py convention (reserved @example.* short-circuit, dark HTML, per-invoice audit row). Dedup via db.payment_recovery_emails.find_one({invoice_id}) is race-safe enough for Stripe webhook cadence but not strictly atomic — under a concurrent double-delivery of the SAME invoice.payment_failed event, two sends could slip through before the audit row lands. Low risk given Stripe's normal delivery pattern; consider a unique index on invoice_id if this ever ships heavier volume.

routers/payments.py L701: portal-session creation is inside the same try/except as the recovery email — if stripe.billing_portal.Session.create fails, the customer gets no email at all. Acceptable trade-off (an email with a dead link is worse than none) but worth flagging.

Test file has 5 tests, not 6 as the review_request stated — coverage still matches every requested behavior (flag + founder alert + recovery email + dedup + my-plan + missing-sub safety + invoice.paid clear). Minor doc drift only.
test_credentials: none needed — all Stripe/Resend calls mocked
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral dev_users rows keyed by uuid-suffixed test-user-* ids, cleaned up per-test. payment_recovery_emails audit rows for the dedup test are deleted at end of test.
